criteria.evidence_quote: In undisturbed communities, diversity is lower because competitive exclusion happens—the best competitors take over and shade out everyone else. In highly disturbed areas, diversity is low because only fast-growing, hardy pioneer species can survive the constant wipeouts. Intermediate disturbance is highest because it prevents the best competitors from taking over, allowing both pioneer and climax species to coexist. On coral reefs, waves open up space so one type of coral doesn't take over everything.
criteria.decision_explanation: The response correctly explains low diversity in undisturbed communities due to competitive exclusion, low diversity in highly disturbed areas due to survival of only hardy pioneer species, and the intermediate disturbance effect allowing coexistence by preventing dominance. Intermediate: competitive dominants eliminated periodically → patch renewal → fugitive species coexist → highest diversity. Coral reefs: intermediate wave disturbance creates diverse patch mosaic; prevents coral competitive exclusion.
